title: How I Built My First Personal Website with a Raspberry Pi 🧙‍♂️⚡
content:
Back in early 2025, I challenged myself to create a fully functional personal website hosted from my own Raspberry Pi 5. Why? Because I wanted to own my infrastructure, learn more about networking, and prove to myself that I could go full maker mode.

I used a mix of NGINX, a lightweight tunnel via Cloudflare, and some HTML + Vanilla JS magic to make everything work. It wasn’t easy — I struggled with DNS settings, permissions, and power outages 😅 — but it was *so* worth it.

The best part? Everything runs locally from a small device on my desk, and anyone in the world can visit it at braisgf.dev 🚀

Lessons I learned:
- Setting up a static server teaches you a LOT about security.
- Raspberry Pi 5 is powerful enough for web serving.
- Debugging DNS is a rite of passage.

Would I recommend it? Absolutely. If you're a dev or a geek who loves control, give it a shot.

In the future I want to expand it with Node.js APIs, integrate blog posts like this one dynamically, and maybe even host an arcade game built in Unity or Godot. ✨
